These country to country comparisons are more often than not, comparing apples and oranges.
Networth is not liquid assets, it's mostly just Pension and real estate equity.. Which in turn is heavily correlated with age = your pension grows as you get older, you have made more mortgage payments.
You also have the issue of inflated prices in real estate, like Japan prior to the Nikkei bubble popped, real estate in Japan was worth four times the entire real estate market in the US. This in turn meant that Japanese were A LOT richer than Americans - at least on paper.

I think the only way to really do country to country comparisons are not through data, but through observations. What does the cities look like? the houses, the cars on the road, how are people dressed, the shops, etc.
This is not perfect either, but it is better at reflecting reality.
